A new research report from Counterpoint Research projects that consumer wearables will generate more than $1 trillion in cumulative revenue through 2032, with smartwatches and wireless earbuds leading the way. Here are the details.

Smartwatches and wireless earbuds are expected to lead the market

In a report published today, Counterpoint Research said that "the global consumer wearables market is expected to generate more than $1 trillion in total revenue between 2026 and 2032."

Within its categorization of consumer wearables, the report projects that hearables will account for the largest share of cumulative revenue, at approximately $360 billion, followed by smartwatches at $304 billion, and smart glasses at $168 billion.

From the report:

Health patches are expected to generate an additional $120 billion in revenue, followed by smart rings at $44 billion, pendants at $24 billion, smart shoes at $18 billion, and fitness bands at $14 billion. As for smart socks, smart clothing, and smart belts, each category is projected to generate less than $10 billion.

Counterpoint Research noted that revenue growth for consumer wearables is twice the rate of shipment growth, and more notably, the market appears to be gradually shifting from fitness tracking toward preventive health, "where the device alerts users before they even realize something is wrong."

As for Apple, it competes in two of the highest projected revenue categories—namely, AirPods and Apple Watch. Apple is also reportedly developing smart glasses, and there are rumors that the company is exploring screen-less fitness bands and smart rings.

Apple disclosed last month that its "Wearables, Home, and Accessories" category generated $7.88 billion in revenue in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, representing a 6% year-over-year increase and the strongest growth for the category since the fourth quarter of fiscal 2022.

Although this category clearly includes more than just wearables, Apple has been actively expanding into this area as a significant revenue source over the years. Counterpoint estimates that AirPods alone will surpass $100 billion in cumulative revenue in 2026.
